ECG+ integrates with Apple Health to unleash the greatest power of your Apple Watch ECG, by analyzing and calculating heart rate variability (HRV) out of your ECG data, which is widely considered one of the best objective metrics for physical fitness and determining your body’s readiness to perform. Additionally, ECG+ app also provides detailed analysis of heartbeat intervals, including QT/QTc, which is an important indicator of your heart's electrical activity.

HRV refers to the variation in time between successive heartbeats, which is an indicator of the health of the autonomic nervous system. QT interval refers to the time it takes for the heart to recharge between beats, which is important for assessing cardiac health.

With HRV trends you can learn your health level changes. A up hill trend means a better physical fitness level and a down hill indicates you should pay more attention to your overall health. With QT trends you can monitor closely your QT intervals over a period of time and seek healthcare attention whenever a prolonged QT is identified automatically.

Things you can do about your ECG data -
1. Measure intervals and voltages on the ECG rhythm waves
2. Calculate HRV (using RMSSD)
3. View Poincaré plot / R-R interval plot
4. HRV trends
5. Generate PDF report with HRV info
6. Send your ECG report to your healthcare provider

So what is HRV?
HRV is a measure of your autonomic nervous system that is widely considered one of the best objective metrics for physical fitness and determining your body’s readiness to perform.

Although HRV manifests as a function of your heart rate, it actually originates from your nervous system. Your autonomic nervous system, which controls the involuntary aspects of your physiology, has two branches, parasympathetic (deactivating) and sympathetic (activating).

The parasympathetic branch (often referred to as “rest and digest”) handles inputs from internal organs, like digestion or your fingernails and hair growing. It causes a decrease in heart rate. The sympathetic branch (often called “fight or flight”) reflects responses to things like stress and exercise, and increases your heart rate.

Heart rate variability comes from these two competing branches simultaneously sending signals to your heart. If your nervous system is balanced, your heart is constantly being told to beat slower by your parasympathetic system, and beat faster by your sympathetic system. This causes a fluctuation in your heart rate: HRV.

Food intolerance or allergy is a significant and widespread medical problem that can be difficult to diagnose. Food allergy can cause severe symptoms in sensitive individuals and may be life threatening if not correctly diagnosed. In many instances the offending food is easily identified however milder forms of food allergy may be more difficult to diagnose.
            
Food intolerance is a neglected area of medicine because of diagnostic difficulties, non-specific symptoms and the relatively mild nature of the resulting illness; however repeated irritation or inflammation of the gastrointestinal tract may have serious consequences including malabsorption syndromes, small bowel overgrowth, coeliac disease and bowel cancer.
            
Your Food Intolerance is an advanced diagnostic programme that is able to identify food groups and specific foods that may be causing your symptoms.
            
The app works by systematically restricting various food groups and individual foods in your diet over a set period and analysing your food intake and any associated symptoms within the designated time interval. Restrictions are designed to allow a varied and reasonable diet within the allotted time frame. Symptoms are measured for their frequency and severity and are categorised as allergic or intolerant.

The app is designed to operate in three stages.
            
Stage I. You will be asked to assign the foods you would typically eat to 1 of the 8 listed food groups. The app contains a comprehensive list of foods contained in each group. You can add foods to these food groups if the food you normally eat is not listed. You will be asked to exclude one food group each day for a set period of time and the results will be analysed. If a suspect food group is identified you may complete the programme or proceed to the next stage.
            
Stage II. If no food group has been identified you will be asked to repeat the programme excluding one food group for seven days.
            
Stage III. If a suspect food group has been identified you will be asked to select the foods from that food group and exclude one of these foods daily as in Stage I.

During the course of the programme, you will be required to enter data PRIOR TO EACH MEAL. You will be asked to enter food groups or foods you are about to consume and identify and quantify any symptoms you experienced from the PREVIOUS MEAL.
            
At the end of the diagnostic programme, your food intake and symptoms will be analysed. You will be presented with a report which lists any identified suspect food groups and foods, and whether your symptoms are suggestive of intolerance or allergy.

The diagnostic programme once started, will take a number of weeks to complete. If you are diligent in recording your foods and not eating the prohibited foods as instructed, this programme will take roughly one month to complete. For individuals with more complex allergies or intolerance the programme may take 2 to 3 months to complete.

Please note that this app is only intended for people who have experienced symptoms of food intolerance or allergy for a number of months.

This programme is a simple, yet effective way to determine any food intolerances or allergies that you may have, so don't wait, download it now!
